name: Sani
confidence_why: Known only second-hand: 西田龍雄 1964 reports the tone system after another work; the primary description was not read.
catalog_citation: 西田龍雄 (Nishida Tatsuo). 1964. ビルマ語とロロ諸語――その声調体系の比較研究――. 東南アジア研究 1(4): 13-28. doi:10.20495/tak.1.4_13
catalog_locator: p. 16, §4 tone-system table and fn. 6; fn. 3 on p. 14 gives Ma Xueliang 1951 撒尼彝語研究 as the source of the Nyi forms; p. 18 on the 55/11 split
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

tone_statements.citation: 金田一春彦 Kindaichi Haruhiko. 1965. 高さのアクセントはアクセントにあらず [Pitch accent and stress accent]. 言語研究 (Gengo Kenkyu) 48: 1-12.
tone_statements.quote: それから,馬学良の"撒尼彜語研究"のp.11によると,サニイ語という中国奥地の言語では/m/という音節は最高の平調で唱えれば「馬」の意,高の平調で唱えれば「吹」の意,低の平調で唱えれば「作」の意,最低の平調で唱えれば「天」の意になるという。このとおりならばこの言語も四段組織だ。
tone_statements.translation: Further, according to p. 11 of Ma Xueliang's 'Sani Yiyu yanjiu', in Sani, a language of the Chinese interior, the syllable /m/ means 'horse' when said on the highest level tone, 'blow' on the high level tone, 'make' on the low level tone and 'sky' on the lowest level tone. If that is so, this language too has a four-level organisation.
tone_statements.locator: p. 3, within note (11) (the passage immediately precedes '注(12)')
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)

tone_statements.citation: 西田龍雄 (Nishida Tatsuo). 1964. ビルマ語とロロ諸語――その声調体系の比較研究―― [Burmese and the Lolo languages: a comparative study of their tone systems]. 東南アジア研究 (Southeast Asian Studies, Kyoto University) 1(4): 13-28.
tone_statements.quote: まず，ここで取り上げるロロ語ニー方言，アヒ方言，ハニ語，リス語およびビルマ語の声調6）体系を掲げて，比較される対象を明らかにしておきたい。[table row] ロロ語，ニー方言: 高平型 55 / 半高型 44 / 中平型 33 / 低平型 11 / 短平型 … 五声 [Axi 五声, Hani 五声, Lisu 六声, Burmese 四声] … 以下の声調表記は，ニー・アヒ・ハニ語は声調型を用い，リス語とビルマ語は声調類で示した。 … (p. 18) ニー方言では初頭に○-n-をもつ単語は高平型55をとり，そのほかは低平型11になったと推定できる。
tone_statements.translation: First, I set out the tone systems of the Lolo Nyi dialect, the Ahi dialect, Hani, Lisu and Burmese taken up here, so as to make clear what is being compared. [table row] Lolo, Nyi dialect: high-level type 55 / half-high type 44 / mid-level type 33 / low-level type 11 / short-level type ... five tones [Axi five, Hani five, Lisu six, Burmese four] ... In the tone notation below, tone values are used for Nyi, Ahi and Hani, and tone classes for Lisu and Burmese. ... (p. 18) In the Nyi dialect, words with an initial nasal prefix took the high-level 55 and the others became low-level 11, we may infer.
tone_statements.locator: p. 16 (section 4 and the tone-system table) and p. 18 as S says; footnote 3 identifying Nyi = Ma 1951 撒尼彝語研究 is on p. 14 (not p. 15).
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)

sources.citation: Bi Xian 毕贤. 2026. 石林撒尼彝语基数词变调研究 [Research on the Transposition of Base Number Words in Shilin Sani Yi Language]. 现代语言学 Modern Linguistics 14(8): 811-817. doi:10.12677/ml.2026.148845
sources.note: Silent on stress (no 重音/轻声/韵律 anywhere). Sec. 2 compares the Shilin Sani phoneme systems of Ma 1951 (44 initials, 19 finals, 5 tones 55/44/33/11/2), Kong 2002 (41/16/5 tones, short tone 2 > 31) and Zhou 2013 (41 initials, 31 finals, 3 tones 55/33/21); sec. 3 describes numeral tone sandhi 55+33 > 33+33, 55+55 > 33+55 conditioned by the following syllable's tone.

sources.citation: Iwasa, Kazue 岩佐一枝. 2021. A Preliminary Report on Entomological Vocabulary in Sani Yi. Journal of Research Institute (Kobe City University of Foreign Studies) 61: 85-108.
sources.note: Silent on stress. Footnote 6 (p. 88) summarises Vial (1909: (5)-(8)) phonology: consonant and vowel letters and five tones ('first tone.. clearly high'.. sources.citation: Ostapirat, Weera. 1996. Sani's Fortis See-Saw and initial devoicing. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 19(1): 59-64. doi:10.15144/LTBA-19.1.59
sources.note: Historical phonology of Sani initials/tones from Ma 1951 data (image PDF, scanned). No statement on Sani word stress; only a closing speculation (p. 63) that Tai/Cantonese kept codas 'due to their final stress'.

sources.citation: Vial, Paul. 1898. Les Lolos: histoire, religion, moeurs, langue, écriture. Shanghai: Imprimerie de la Mission catholique (Études sino-orientales, fasc. A). [data = dialecte gni, i.e. Sani]
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Ch. III 'De la langue des Lolos' (pp. 13-15) treats syllable shape (CV, no codas) and word order; tone is mentioned only in passing (p. 14 negative ma 'au second ton'; pp. 39-40 'le même mot ba pourra se prononcer sur le ton haut, bas, bref ou long'; p. 66 'je n'ai marqué aucun ton.. il faut bien faire attention aux accents' where 'accents' = French diacritics on vowels, not stress).

sources.note: Describes another variety (Glottolog lolo1265). No Sani tone data of its own. Sani (撒尼彝語 / ロロ語ニー方言) enters only in one retrospective sentence on p. 873 saying that the author's 1964 paper set up regular correspondences among Nyi (Sani), Ahi, Hani, Lisu and Burmese 'especially by the comparison of tones', plus one cognate label 'Nyi-lolo' in fn. 25 (p. 881). The article is a review of Burling 1967 Proto Lolo-Burmese: Burmese tone/final problem (pp. 869-871), a five-step programme with '(Burmese) Lolo-Hani comparison' as step 4 (p. 875), and Burmese-Atsi-Maru tone correspondence classes (p. 888…

tone.quote: 撒尼彝語，阿細語，哈尼語の資料を使って，私は1958年に，ロロ語とビルマ語の比較研究を試み，1964年にとくに声調の比較によってロロ語ニー方言，アヒ方言，ハニ語，リス語とビルマ語の問の規則的な対応関係と共通形式の設定を行なった。しかし，なお本当の意味でのロロ系言語とビル系言語の中間的な性格を示す，ラフ語・アカ語の信頼できる資料はなかった。
tone.locator: p. 873, first paragraph after the Shafer/Wolfenden discussion. Quoted from the with inter-character spacing and line breaks removed; the superscript footnote call-outs 17 and 18 (pointing to Nishida 1958 and to 'ビルマ語とロロ諸語' 1964) are omitted; '問' is the 's reading of printed 間, and 'なかった' is re-joined from 'なか／マっ／た'.
tone.translation: Using the Sani Yi, Axi and Hani materials, I attempted a comparative study of Lolo and Burmese in 1958, and in 1964, especially through the comparison of tones, I set up the regular correspondences and common forms among the Lolo Nyi dialect, the Ahi dialect, Hani, Lisu and Burmese. However, there were still no reliable materials for Lahu and Akha, the languages that show a truly intermediate character between the Lolo-type and the Burmese-type languages.

sources.note: Among 11 Ngwi clusters a rising tone developed from a historically high tone in nine; prevocalic consonants conditioned splits in some. Sani (Shilin county seat, wordlist from Chen 2010; Appendix 1 row 51, Central/Sanoid, type AB) is one comparison lect; its reflexes in Appendix 3 are level/falling only (*1 33, *2 21~55 by initial type, *3 33, *H 33, *L 2~55), i.e. no rising tone. Tone values in the accompanying CLDF transcription (lexibank yangyi, 699 Sani forms): 33 x344, 44 x256, 21 x237, 55 x138, short 2 x90 (S's token counts are exactly double). Paper body not opened (closed access).

Treat as a comparative pointer; tone content for Sani to be checked in print.

Yi dialectology textbook (430 pp.) covering the six Yi dialect areas incl. the Southeastern dialect (撒尼); such handbooks normally give 声母/韵母/声调 tables per representative point, but the Sani tone coverage is unverified. a later reading confirmed over the whole archive.org text that the supposed open scan is a different (1803, English) book, so this remains a print-only pointer for a librarian (CiNii member libraries; NYPL/WorldCat per OCLC 70873661), not an archive.org retrieval.
